segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Hello?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Hi.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: It's Laura Cariton here.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: We've just arrived at the holiday flat, but I can't get the hot water and heating to work.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Oh right!

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: That's easy.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Don't worry.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: In the upstairs cupboard, you'll find the water heater.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: You'll see three main controls on the left at the bottom of the heater.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: The first one - the round one on the far left - is the most important one for the heating and hot water.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: It's the main control switch. Make sure it's in the 'on' position.The switch is 'off'.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: That's probably what's happened - it's got switched off by mistake

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: The middle one of these three controls - you'll see it's slightly larger than the first one - controls the radiators.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: If you feel cold while you're there and need the radiators on, this needs to be turned to maximum.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: The last of the three controls - the one on the right - is usually on about a number four setting which for the water in the taps is usually quite hot enough.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Below the heating controls in the middle is a small round plastic button. If there isn't enough water in the pipes, sometimes the heater goes out.If this happens you'll need to press this button to reset the heater. Hold it in for about five seconds and the heater should come on again.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Then there's a little square indicator under the third knob that's kind of alarm light. It'll flash if you need to reset the heater.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: It sounds complicated...

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: I'm sure you won't have any problems with it.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: There should be some more instructions on the side of the heater.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Call me back if you can't make it work.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Okay.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: While you're on the phone, we haven't managed to find a few things we need, like extra pillows for the beds and some washing powder.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Is there any here?

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Pillows... yes.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: If you look in the cupboard, the large white one upstairs - to the left of the bathroom door - there should be four or five on the top shelf. And if you want to do some washing, there's some powder for that... probably by the back door.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: There's a kind of shelf there above the sink. In fact, I'm sure there's some there, in a large blue box.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: You need about half a cup full for each wash.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: And that reminds me, the spare key to the back door is hanging on a hook on the wall by the sitting room window. Please make sure to put it back when you've used it.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: The previous guests lost it in the garden and I had to find some spare bulbs in a large cardboard box.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: It's on top of the washing machine with all kinds of useful things in it.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Oh, and another thing I forgot to mention when we last spoke...

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Yes?

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: I've left you a local map, so you'll be able to find your way around easily.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: It shows the whole area.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: I put it in the top drawer of the chest under the TV in your bedroom.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: There's a whole file of local information in there too.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Thanks.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: What about visiting the town?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Can you give us any advice?

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Yes.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: You'll need to take the car.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: It's too far to walk from the flat really.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: You have to pay to leave your car in all the car parks now I'm afraid...

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: I like the one that's by the station best and you can walk to the town centre from there in five minutes.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: That's where all the best restaurants are.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: But if you want a takeaway, the Italian one does really good pasta and pizzas.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Call 7-3 double 2.8-1 for that one, or 7 double 6, double 1,9 for the Chinese.They's both good and they'll both deliver to the flat.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: As for places to visit, yes, do go and see the railway museum.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: The exhibition is small but really good.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: It gets very crowded on Sundays, so I suggest you visit it on a quieter day, later in the week, but not on Thursdays which is market day - you won't find anywhere to park and it's also the only day of the week when they're not open! Anything else?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Not for the moment.Thanks!
